title: Integrated Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition
author: Daniel Rivera
content:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standardized processes and controls for budgeting & forecasting, procurement, contracts, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement owners, hiring managers, and approvers. The goal is to ensure clear approval paths, consistent accounting treatment (ASC 606 principles), timely billing, and defensible audit trails.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood business units and subsidiaries.
- Covers: annual budgeting, quarterly reforecast, purchase requests and POs, vendor onboarding, contract lifecycle (NDA, MSA, SOW), invoicing, revenue recognition, credit memos, and billing disputes.

Key Principles
1. Segregation of duties: requestor, approver, and accounting/finance are distinct roles.
2. Documentation: every spend and contract must have an associated PO/contract ID and digital record.
3. Materiality thresholds and controls scale with spend.
4. Revenue follows performance obligations and evidence of transfer per ASC 606.

Roles & Owners
- Finance (Owner): overall budgeting process, revenue recognition, month-end close, audit support.
- Legal (Owner): contract template maintenance, legal review, risk acceptance.
- Procurement (Owner): vendor sourcing, KYC, purchase order issuance.
- Requesting Manager: initiates requisition, provides business justification and cost center.
- Approver(s): managers / finance approvers per approval matrix.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting
Overview
The budgeting process ties headcount, committed capacity (Dedicated contracts), cloud & GPU spend, R&D programs, and GTM investments to company targets. Forecasting is a continuous process with defined monthly, quarterly, and annual cadences.

Annual Budget Cycle (timeline)
- Sep–Oct: Planning kickoff, departmental targets issued by Finance.
- Oct–Nov: Department budgets submitted with headcount plans, vendor commitments, and capital requests.
- Dec: Leadership reviews and finalizes budget.
- Jan 1: New fiscal budget effective.

Quarterly Reforecast
- Mid-quarter: preliminary reforecast.
- Two weeks prior to quarter close: final reforecast submitted.
- Reforecasts must include: updated headcount plan, committed vendor spend, pipeline-driven revenue changes, and any one-time items.

Budget Approval Matrix
- Up to $10,000: Manager approval.
- $10,001–$100,000: Director / Finance approval.
- $100,001–$1,000,000: VP + Finance approval.
- > $1,000,000: CFO + CEO approval and Board notification (if impacts ARR/growth targets).

Capital vs Operating Spend
- Capital requests (hardware, multi-year licenses): submit capex request form and justification; Finance will run CAPEX amortization schedule.
- Operating spend: charged to current period and included in monthly P&L.

Key Deliverables & Metrics
- Monthly variance report: budget vs actual by cost center (due 7 business days after month close).
- Cash runway projection: updated weekly by FP&A.
- Headcount tracker: reconciled monthly with People Ops.

2) Procurement Procedures
Purchase Request to PO (standard flow)
1. Requestor creates a Purchase Requisition (PR) in the procurement portal (include vendor, business justification, cost center, GL code, expected delivery date).
2. Procurement validates vendor status (existing vs new).
3. Approvals routed per Approval Matrix above.
4. Procurement issues Purchase Order (PO) once approved.
5. Goods/services delivered; requestor confirms receipt in portal.
6. Vendor invoices referencing PO are sent to billing@redwoodinference.com.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist (new vendors)
- Vendor profile in procurement system (name, tax ID, contact, bank details).
- W-9 / local tax form.
- AML/KYC checks for partner classification.
- Insurance certificate (if required).
- Signed onboarding documents (NDA/MSA) where applicable.
- Payment terms established (Net 30 default).

Procurement Controls & Exceptions
- NO verbal approvals for purchases > $25,000 — written approval required.
- Split-purchase rule: do not split orders to circumvent approval limits. Procurement will reject and escalate.
- Emergency purchases: allow expedited process with CFO sign-off and retrospective PO issuance within 48 hours.

Preferred Vendor & Contracted Discounts
- Procurement maintains a preferred vendor list with negotiated pricing, volume discounts, and term discounts. Check the vendor catalog before sourcing.

3) Contracts & Legal Process
Contract Lifecycle
- Templates: Legal maintains MSA, SOW, NDA, Data Processing Agreement (DPA), and reseller agreements in the contract repository. Use the current template; redlines must be tracked in DocuSign/Confluence.
- Initiation: Requestor fills Contract Intake Form with key commercial terms (scope, term, fees, termination, data residency needs).
- Legal Review: Legal performs risk assessment and assigns change flags (A: standard, B: moderate risk, C: high risk).
- Signature: DocuSign is the default execution method. The signatory authority is per Delegation of Authority (DoA).
- Storage: Executed contracts are stored in the central contract repository (SharePoint/Box) and indexed in procurement system with contract ID.

Contract Review SLAs
- Standard MSA/NDA: Legal turnaround 3 business days.
- High-risk or custom terms: 7–15 business days depending on complexity.

Contract Approvals & Escalation Matrix
- Commercial value < $200k and standard legal terms: Sales/Finance negotiator sign-off + Legal acknowledgement.
- Commercial value >= $200k or non-standard terms: Legal + VP Finance + Sales Leadership.
- Data sovereignty or security exceptions: escalate to Security & Compliance and Legal leadership.

Third-party Data & Security Requirements
- For any contract involving customer data, attach the DPA and ensure security questionnaire completion (via Security & Compliance).
- If vendor requires access to production systems, a separate technical access review and SSO onboarding is required.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Principles (ASC 606-aligned)
- Identify the contract(s) with the customer.
- Identify the performance obligations.
- Determine the transaction price.
- Allocate the transaction price to performance obligations.
- Recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation.

Common Scenarios
- Hosted API usage (metered): Revenue recognized as usage occurs (per invoice period).
- Dedicated capacity / reserved contracts (term commitments): Recognize over time ratably over the service period unless evidence supports another pattern.
- Implementation or professional services (one-time): Recognize upon completion of the stated deliverable or over time if criteria met.

Billing & Invoice Process
- Billing cadence: Monthly for hosted API and usage; quarterly or annually for reserved capacity as contract dictates.
- Invoicing: Finance issues invoices within 5 business days after period close.
- Payment terms: Net 30 default; exceptions must be recorded on the customer contract and approved by VP Finance.
- Electronic delivery: Send invoices via the customer’s preferred electronic billing system or email to accounts-payable as provided.

Deferred Revenue & Contract Liabilities
- Payments received in advance are recorded as Deferred Revenue / Contract Liabilities until revenue recognition criteria are met.
- Revenue deferrals must be reconciled monthly to the contract ledger and reviewed by FP&A during close.

Credit Memos & Billing Disputes
- Dispute escalation: Customer raises dispute via billing@redwoodinference.com. Finance triages within 3 business days.
- Credits: Issued as credit memos referencing the original invoice and contract ID. Approval for credit > $10,000 requires VP Finance sign-off.

Revenue Cutover & Migration (e.g., plan changes)
- For upgrades/downgrades mid-period, pro-rate revenue recognition based on performance obligations and agreed commercial terms. Document changes with amendment and updated SOW or billing schedule.

Accounting Close & Audit Support
- Month-end close checklist: all invoices posted, all cash receipts applied, deferred revenue reconciled, reconciliations approved by FP&A.
- Audit artifacts: maintain contract copies, billing schedules, proof-of-delivery/usage reports, and approval logs for at least 7 years (or local statutory requirement).

Controls, KPIs & Monitoring
- KPIs: DSO (target <= 40 days), Invoice accuracy rate (target >= 99%), Time-to-issue invoice (<= 5 business days), Forecast accuracy (quarterly MAPE <= 6%).
- Internal control: periodic review of manual journals, segregation of duties, and quarterly SOX readiness checks for material processes.

Appendices
A. Forms & Templates
- Purchase Requisition template (procurement portal).
- Contract Intake Form (Confluence link).
- CapEx Request Form.

B. Quick Reference Approval Matrix (summary)
- Manager: up to $10k
- Director: $10k–$100k
- VP + Finance: $100k–$1M
- CFO + CEO: > $1M

C. Frequently Asked Questions
- Q: Who signs MSAs?
  A: Delegation of Authority table defines signatory by contract value and type; default sales rep cannot sign > $200k.
- Q: How are usage disputes handled?
  A: Provide signed usage logs or telemetry within 10 business days. Finance will review and issue credit or corrected invoice.
